answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-reusable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits prove duplicate claims or fabricated work. This does not make identities impossible to fake; it makes influence costly: an attacker must tie up capital in every Sybil and risks losing it on detection. Reputation can then accrue only to stake-backed work, whether the task is mapping an oasis, composing a sonnet, or sending a whisper.
